newsitem.title: USA: Brunswick cites new products, acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Brunswick cites new products, acquisitions.

text.p: Brunswick Corp said Monday that record 1997 second quarter results, including a $1 billion in sales, benefitted from new products and acquisitions.

"Quarterly sales topped $1 billion for the first time reflecting growth in our core businesses through new product introductions and effective marketing, and benefiting from acquisitions designed to expand our family of branded consumer products for the active recreation enthusiast," said Brunswick Chairman and Chief Executive Peter Larson in a news release.

Earlier today, Brunswick reported a 19 percent increase in second quarter earnings from continuing operations to a record $82.9 million, or $0.83 per share on a 17 percent sales gain for the second quarter of 1997.

Recreation segment sales for the quarter increased 59 percent to $349.1 million, and operating earnings rose 75 percent to $41.7 million. Sales of fishing equipment rose and shipments of bowling equipment increased, primarily in the growing Asian markets.

In the past 12 months, Brunswick acquired the Roadmaster and Mongoose bicycle businesses, Igloo coolers, Hoppe's line of hunting accessories, and Life Fitness cardiovascular and strength training equipment.
In the second quarter, the recreation segment businesses accounted for about 35 percent of total sales, up from 26 percent a year ago."
Marine segment sales were up three percent in the second quarter to $659.1 million, and operating earnings were up seven percent to $105.8 million.

Headquartered in Lake Forest, Illinois, Brunswick is a multinational company serving outdoor and indoor active recreation markets with consumer products that include such leading brands as Zebco and Quantum fishing reels and reel/rod combinations; American Camper and Remington camping gear; Igloo coolers and ice chests; Mongoose, Roadmaster and Ride Hard bicycles; Brunswick bowling and family entertainment centers, equipment and consumer products; Brunswick billiards tables; Life Fitness cardiovascular and strength training equipment.

Also, Sea Ray, Bayliner and Maxum pleasure boats, Baja high-performance boats, Boston Whaler and Trophy offshore fishing boats; Mercury, Mariner and Force outboard engines and MerCruiser sterndrives and inboard engines.

Forward looking statements, as defined by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Law, involve certain risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from expectations as of the date of this announcement. These risks include, but are not limited to, adverse weather conditions retarding sales; inventory adjustments by major retailers; competitive pricing pressures; success of planned acquisitions, marketing and cost-management programs and shifts in market demand.
